transcript.text:
I can help with that. To narrow this down quickly: is the freezer compartment still cold (frozen solid), or is it warm as well? This tells us if the fridge is just not getting air from a working freezer, or if the whole cooling system has stopped.
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
freezer's still freezing, food solid. just the fridge warm, milk going off

[Heading: Airflow blockage or fan fault]
That pattern—freezer cold but fridge warm—is classic for an airflow issue. The freezer is producing the cold, but it isn't reaching the fridge section. This usually happens because the vent letting cold air through is blocked by food or ice, or because the internal fan that pushes the air has stopped. Please check the back wall inside the fridge compartment. Are there vents (grilles) where cold air enters from the freezer? Is food blocking them, or can you see any ice build-up around these vents?
moved the food away from the back, no difference. hardly any cold air from the slots

[Heading: Blocked defrost drain or internal ice blockage]
The most common cause for this specific pattern (freezer cold, fridge warm) is a blocked defrost drain or ice building up behind the back panel, which chokes the air passage. Please check the bottom of the back wall inside the fridge compartment. There should be a small drain hole (sometimes hidden under a plastic grille). Is it clear, or can you see water/ice blocking it? If you are unsure what to look for, let me know and I will guide you through a manual defrost.
can't see a drain hole in the fridge part. there's a thick layer of white frost on the back wall of the freezer though, more than I've ever seen. happy to do the manual defrost

[Heading: Defrost system failure causing ice blockage]
1. Switch the appliance off at the wall socket and unplug it.
2. Remove all food and store it safely in cool bags or another fridge.
3. Leave both doors wide open and place towels on the floor to catch the meltwater.
4. Leave it for 24 hours until all ice has melted completely. Do not try to chip the ice away with sharp objects as you could damage the cooling pipes.
5. Once dry, plug it back in and leave it running for at least 6 hours before putting food back in. If the fridge cools down normally after this but the thick frost returns within a few days, we will need to check the defrost heater or thermostat, as one of those components has likely failed.
did the defrost. fridge got cold again within a day, 3C. but after about 5 days it's starting to creep up again

[Heading: Defrost system failure (heater or thermostat)]
The fact that cooling returned after the defrost but then failed again within 5 days confirms a recurring ice build-up. This is almost certainly caused by a fault in the automatic defrost system—most likely the defrost heater has burned out or the defrost thermostat (thermal fuse) has failed, meaning the appliance can no longer melt the normal frost that builds up on the evaporator coils. To distinguish this from an evaporator fan failure, please listen inside the freezer when the compressor is running. Do you hear a steady humming or whirring sound? If you open the door slightly and the sound stops, it’s definitely the fan (which confirms airflow is blocked by ice). If it is silent even with the door shut, the heater/thermostat is the primary suspect. Once we confirm this pattern, the fix will require replacing the failed defrost component. This involves opening the rear panel of the freezer to access the coils and testing/replacing parts like the heater or thermal fuse.
can hear a faint scraping/ticking noise from the freezer sometimes. motor running a lot too. not sure about a steady hum

[Heading: Defect in the automatic defrost system (heater or thermostat)]
The scraping noise you hear is likely the evaporator fan blade hitting ice that has built up behind the back panel because it didn't melt during the last cycle. The fact that cooling returned after your manual defrost but failed again within 5 days confirms that the automatic defrost system has stopped working—most commonly due to a burnt-out defrost heater or a failed defrost thermostat (thermal fuse). Because these parts are located inside the freezer's rear panel and require electrical testing and replacement, this is not an owner-safe repair. You should contact a qualified appliance engineer to replace the faulty component.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
